name: EDATE
description: EDATE returns the date that is a given number of months before or after a start date, preserving the day of the month and rolling to the last day when that day does not exist in the target month.
tldr: Shifts a date by a number of months.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: The number of months to move. Positive moves forward, negative moves backward. The value is truncated to an integer.

basicExample.description: Three months after a mid-January date

advancedExamples.title: End-of-month rollover in a leap year
advancedExamples.description: February has no 31st, so it rolls to the last day
advancedExamples.explanation: 2024 is a leap year, so February's last day is the 29th (serial 45350).

advancedExamples.title: Moving backward
advancedExamples.description: A negative months value goes to the past

howItWorks: EDATE adds the specified number of months to start_date. It keeps the same day number; if that day is invalid in the resulting month (for example the 31st of February), Excel returns the last day of that month. The result is a date serial.

howToSteps.name: Enter the start date
howToSteps.text: Provide a date serial or DATE(...) expression.

howToSteps.name: Enter the month offset
howToSteps.text: Use a positive or negative integer for months.

howToSteps.name: Format as a date
howToSteps.text: The result is a serial; apply a date format to view it.

limitations: The day of month is preserved but rolls to the last day if the target month is shorter.
The months argument is truncated to an integer (1.9 becomes 1).
The result is a serial number and needs a date format to be readable.

commonErrors.cause: The start_date is not a valid date serial.
commonErrors.fix: Pass a real date value or DATE(...) expression.

commonErrors.cause: The original day does not exist in the target month.
commonErrors.fix: This is expected; EDATE returns the last valid day of that month.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: EDATE works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and rollover behavior.

faq.question: What happens on Jan 31 plus one month?
faq.answer: It returns Feb 28 (or Feb 29 in a leap year) because February has no 31st.

faq.question: Can months be negative?
faq.answer: Yes, a negative value moves the date backward in time.

faq.question: Does EDATE change the day?
faq.answer: It keeps the same day unless that day is invalid in the new month, then it uses the last day.
